articles.title: NASA Shares Plans to Accelerate Artemis, Return to Moon
articles.description: In an update on Oct. 23, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman and other agency leaders shared the agency’s path to returning Americans to the lunar surface in 2028. Agency leadership provided updates on the previously announced acceleration plans for the Artemis program, advancing toward the agency’s Artemis III test flight in 2027 and Artemis IV Moon […]
articles.summary: NASA announces an accelerated timeline for the Artemis program, bringing humanity's return to the Moon closer than previously planned.

articles.title: A cosmic 'leaf blower': Light-propelled winds help explain early universe's bright galaxies
articles.description: When astronomers looked at photos of the early universe taken by the James Webb Space Telescope, they found something odd: an overabundance of bright galaxies. Based on what they knew about the early universe, such galaxies should have been far less common in the few hundred million years following the Big Bang.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: James Webb Space Telescope observations reveal that light-propelled winds help explain the unexpected brightness of galaxies in the early universe, solving a major cosmic mystery.

articles.title: NASA smashed into an asteroid. Now Hera is closing in to see what happened
articles.description: Europe’s Hera spacecraft has captured its first clear view of two asteroids involved in NASA’s historic 2022 experiment to redirect a potentially dangerous space rock. Now approaching the pair, Hera will investigate the mysterious aftermath of the collision and uncover why the asteroid shifted far more than scientists predicted.
articles.summary: Europe's Hera spacecraft has captured detailed images of the asteroids involved in NASA's historic 2022 kinetic impact experiment, furthering our understanding of planetary defense.

articles.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 is about to reach a historic one-light-day milestone
articles.description: NASA’s Voyager 1 is approaching an extraordinary milestone nearly 50 years after its launch, even as engineers battle dwindling power and mysterious technical problems. A clever energy-saving maneuver has extended the spacecraft’s scientific mission, while an unexplained 48-hour communications blackout recently gave NASA a scare. On November 18, Voyager 1 will reach a distance of one light-day from Earth, making even the simplest round-trip communication take 48 hours.
articles.summary: NASA's Voyager 1 is approaching a historic one-light-day milestone nearly 50 years after launch, continuing its unprecedented journey as humanity's most distant spacecraft.

articles.title: All 5 genetic “letters” of DNA and RNA discovered in a 4.5-billion-year-old asteroid
articles.description: Scientists have discovered all five essential nucleobases used in DNA and RNA in pristine samples from asteroid Ryugu, revealing that key ingredients for life existed in space billions of years ago. The remarkable finding adds to growing evidence from other asteroids and meteorites that these molecules were widespread throughout the early Solar System.
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered all five essential nucleobases of DNA and RNA in pristine samples from asteroid Ryugu, providing compelling evidence for the delivery of life's chemical building blocks via cosmic materials.

articles.title: Il y a 26 ans presque jour pour jour, les trois premiers astronautes arrivaient à bord de la Station spatiale internationale : une aventure humaine qui ne s’est jamais interrompue depuis
articles.description: Depuis le 2 novembre 2000, il ne s’est pas écoulé une seule seconde sans qu’un être humain flotte quelque part au-dessus de nos têtes. Hier, l'ISS fêtait ses 26 ans d’occupation sans interruption, soit à peu près 150 000 tours de la Terre accomplis avec au mo…
articles.summary: The International Space Station celebrates 26 years of continuous human presence in orbit, representing an unprecedented achievement in space exploration and international cooperation. Since November 2, 2000, humanity has maintained an unbroken presence in space.

articles.title: APOD: 2026 November 5 – Enceladus in Silhouette
articles.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 5 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss   APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Enceladus in Silhouette […]
articles.summary: NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day features Enceladus silhouetted against Saturn, showcasing one of the solar system's most intriguing icy moons.

articles.title: NASA Navigation Experiment Shows Promise for Planetary Landings
articles.description: NASA successfully demonstrated technology designed to help spacecraft autonomously navigate to safe landing sites on the Moon and on other planets. An Alta-X drone equipped with the agency’s Safe and Precise Landing – Integrated Capabilities Evolution (SPLICE) guidance, navigation, and control payload completed simulated lunar descent and landing maneuvers Aug. 27. The flight took place […]
articles.summary: NASA successfully demonstrates autonomous landing navigation technology that will enable spacecraft to safely land on planetary surfaces.

articles.title: Hubble Reveals Cosmic Mystery
articles.description: This photo released on Nov. 2, 2026, showcases NGC  4449, a dwarf irregular. Researchers using NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope studied 37 nearby dwarf galaxies — small galaxies containing a few thousand to hundreds of millions of stars — including NGC 4449 and found that much of the oxygen they expected to see is missing. Read […]
articles.summary: The Hubble Space Telescope captures a stunning image of NGC 4449, a dwarf irregular galaxy, revealing new insights into galactic structure and evolution.

articles.title: China Unveils Their Plan for a Crewed Moon Landing
articles.description: Yesterday, on November 3rd, the deputy chief designer of China's crewed space program and chief designer of the lunar exploration program (Wang Xiang) unveiled an official statement detailing its [plans for a crewed mission to the Moon](https://english.spacechina.com/n17212/c4744561/content.html).
articles.summary: China announces its comprehensive plan for a crewed lunar landing, expanding international efforts to establish human presence on the Moon.

articles.title: Giant Impacts Help Rocky Planets Retain Their Atmospheres
articles.description: For a long time, planetary scientists thought that giant impacts drove a young planet's atmosphere away into space with all the heat they generated. But it turns out the opposite could be true. The mass a young planet gains through a giant impact increases its gravitational hold on its atmosphere.
articles.summary: Planetary scientists discover that giant impacts paradoxically help young rocky planets retain their atmospheres, revising previous understanding of planetary formation.

articles.title: A Virtual Lifeless Earth Will Help Scientists Find Life on Exoplanets
articles.description: Researchers have created a model lifeless Earth that couples the atmosphere with interior planetary processes. The model can reproduce Earth's modern habitable state without including life, showing that a planet that appears habitable isn't necessarily inhabited. The tool will be useful when and if the Habitable Worlds Observatory is launched, by helping identify false positives.
articles.summary: Researchers create a virtual lifeless Earth model to better identify biosignatures and detect life on distant exoplanets.

articles.title: The Vera Rubin Has Found Two More of the Milky Way's Dim Satellites
articles.description: The Vera Rubin Observatory has detected two more of the Milky Ways' dim, hard to see satellites. One is an ultra-faint dwarf galaxy, and one is a globular cluster. Each one is a missing piece of the puzzle in the Milky Way's merger history. By finding more of these satellites, our understanding of galaxy growth, and the role dark matter plays in it, will improve.
articles.summary: The Vera Rubin Observatory has discovered two additional ultra-faint satellite galaxies orbiting the Milky Way, advancing our understanding of galactic structure and dark matter distribution.

articles.title: European orbiter detects fresh hints of volcanic activity on Mars
articles.description: New evidence from gas seeping above volcanic rifts suggests Mars is not geologically dead deep inside, but merely sleeping. Fresh fissures along the Alba Mons region hint at active spots under the surface, where gases from inside the planet may be making their way up to the surface.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: European spacecraft have detected fresh evidence of volcanic activity on Mars, revealing that the planet remains geologically dynamic beneath its surface.

articles.title: Cosmic hydrogen measurement marks breakthrough in mapping the universe
articles.description: An international research project is bringing scientists closer to mapping the universe. The MeerKLASS Collaboration has reported its first measurement of the large-scale clustering of cosmic hydrogen, advancing a technique that could transform how cosmologists chart the universe.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: The MeerKLASS Collaboration has achieved a breakthrough in cosmic hydrogen measurement, bringing scientists closer to comprehensive three-dimensional mapping of the universe.

articles.title: Pulsars set first mass limits on supermassive black hole pairs in the early universe
articles.description: So far, observations by instruments including the James Webb Space Telescope have revealed the presence of surprisingly massive black holes in the early universe. Even less than a billion years after the Big Bang, some of these bodies already weighed billions of times the mass of the sun, and to date, astronomers are unclear as to how they could have grown so large so quickly.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Pulsar observations combined with James Webb Space Telescope data have set the first mass limits on supermassive black hole pairs in the early universe, revealing surprising early cosmic evolution.

articles.title: Giant planet emerges from two-year-old JWST data thanks to glare-removal technique
articles.description: Even the world's most powerful telescopes have their blind spots. Although NASA's James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) can peer billions of years into the past, it still struggles to photograph planets orbiting nearby stars. Stars shine with such extraordinary brightness that their glare overwhelms nearby planets' faint glow.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: A newly developed glare-removal technique has enabled astronomers to discover a giant planet hidden in two-year-old JWST data, expanding exoplanet detection capabilities.

articles.title: NASA is racing against time to save the Hubble Space Telescope
articles.description: NASA is exploring a daring plan to save the legendary Hubble Space Telescope from its eventual fiery plunge into Earth's atmosphere. After more than 35 years of groundbreaking discoveries, Hubble is slowly losing altitude, and without intervention, it could fall back to Earth as early as 2033 or 2034. To keep the iconic observatory operating, NASA is asking private space companies to propose innovative ways to boost Hubble into a higher orbit, upgrade its capabilities, or safely dispose of it when its mission finally ends.
articles.summary: NASA is pursuing an ambitious plan to extend the life of the legendary Hubble Space Telescope and prevent its eventual reentry, ensuring continued groundbreaking observations.

articles.title: A hidden star is plowing through Betelgeuse’s atmosphere, new evidence suggests
articles.description: Something mysterious is disturbing Betelgeuse, and astronomers believe they have identified the culprit: a hidden companion star called Siwarha. New radio observations reveal that the smaller star may be plowing through Betelgeuse’s enormous atmosphere, creating disturbances that subtly stretch and distort the red supergiant’s shape.
articles.summary: Astronomers have identified evidence of a hidden companion star plowing through Betelgeuse's atmosphere, explaining mysterious disturbances in the red supergiant's behavior.

articles.title: NASA’s Perseverance Mars rover breaks historic record after traveling 28 miles
articles.description: NASA’s Perseverance rover has set a historic record by traveling 28.10 miles across Mars, farther than any vehicle has ever driven on another world. Armed with groundbreaking autonomous navigation technology and increasingly advanced driving capabilities, the rover is pushing the boundaries of robotic exploration.
articles.summary: NASA's Perseverance rover has set a historic distance record by traveling 28.10 miles across Mars, surpassing all previous rover achievements on the Red Planet.

articles.title: IceCube detects ghost particles with 10 billion times the energy of solar neutrinos
articles.description: Mysterious particles called neutrinos constantly stream through our bodies, and scientists are now detecting incredibly powerful versions arriving from distant cosmic sources using a massive observatory buried in Antarctic ice. These elusive “ghost particles” could hold extraordinary clues about the Big Bang, extreme cosmic events, and some of the universe’s greatest mysteries.
articles.summary: The IceCube detector has captured ghost particles (neutrinos) with energies 10 billion times greater than solar neutrinos, opening new windows into high-energy cosmic phenomena.

articles.title: Scientists just found a loophole that could let black holes split in two
articles.description: Scientists have discovered a possible loophole in the laws that normally prevent black holes from splitting apart, suggesting that extremely fast-spinning black holes might divide into two. The surprising finding raises the possibility of an entirely new black hole phenomenon that future telescopes could potentially detect.
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered a theoretical loophole in physics that could allow black holes to split apart, challenging conventional understanding of black hole behavior. This breakthrough expands our knowledge of extreme cosmic objects and their properties.

articles.title: 2 astronauts will finish upgrading ISS solar arrays during spacewalk today: Watch it live
articles.description: NASA's Anil Menon and Canada Joshua Kutryk will install the International Space Station's final roll-out solar array during a spacewalk today (Nov. 5). Here's how to watch it live.
articles.summary: NASA astronauts Anil Menon and Joshua Kutryk are completing the final roll-out solar array upgrade for the International Space Station during a live spacewalk. This milestone enhances the ISS's power capabilities and demonstrates ongoing human spaceflight achievements.

articles.title: Mars isn't dead — recent volcanic activity reveals it's just sleeping
articles.description: Scientists have long suspected that Mars is geologically "dead" but new spacecraft observations suggests the Red Planet's volcanoes are merely sleeping.
articles.summary: Recent spacecraft observations reveal that Mars is geologically active with signs of recent volcanic activity, suggesting the Red Planet is dormant rather than dead. This discovery opens new possibilities for understanding Mars's interior dynamics and past habitability.

articles.title: Nanohertz Gravitational-Wave Constraints on Supermassive Binary Black Holes at Cosmic Dawn
articles.description: Author(s): Yiqin Chen, Shi-Yi Zhao, Xingjiang Zhu, N. D. Ramesh Bhat, Jacob Cardinal Tremblay, Małgorzata Curyło, Valentina Di Marco, George Hobbs, Wenhua Ling, Rami F. Mandow, Richard N. Manchester, Saurav Mishra, Daniel J. Reardon, Sparrow Roch, Christopher…
articles.summary: Researchers have used nanohertz gravitational-wave observations to constrain the properties of supermassive binary black holes at cosmic dawn. This work reveals insights into black hole formation and evolution in the early universe.

articles.title: Two Different Kinds of Gamma-Ray Bursts Erupted 4 Minutes Apart. Astronomers Have Never Seen This Before.
articles.description: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) are among the most energetic cosmic events since the Big Bang, releasing the most energetic type of radiation, gamma rays – the stuff that turned unassuming Bruce Banner into the rampaging Hulk, but on an astronomical, potentially plan…
articles.summary: Astronomers have observed two different types of gamma-ray bursts erupting just 4 minutes apart—an unprecedented cosmic event. This rare occurrence provides new insights into the most energetic phenomena in the universe since the Big Bang.

articles.title: Figuring out where cosmic neutrinos come from is tricky - radio telescopes could help find where these ‘ghost particles’ originate
articles.description: A researcher just won a Nobel Prize for detecting tiny particles from space. Scientists now want to get better at figuring out where in the cosmos they come from.
articles.summary: Radio telescopes are being developed to identify the cosmic origins of ghostly neutrinos from space, building on recent Nobel Prize-winning detection work. This advancement will revolutionize neutrino astronomy and our understanding of cosmic events.

articles.title: Possible dwarf planet discovered beyond Pluto
articles.description: Astronomers have found a large icy object beyond Pluto, dubbed 2026 ED138, that could become the solar system’s sixth dwarf planet Read Full Article at RT.com
articles.summary: Astronomers have discovered a large icy object beyond Pluto, designated 2026 ED138, that could qualify as our solar system's sixth dwarf planet. This significant find expands our understanding of the distant solar system's composition and structure.

articles.title: World's largest digital camera snaps new world beyond Pluto
articles.description: Space was so much simpler when I was a kid. Back in the 1980s, we still hoped to find habitable planets around every star. Nine planets orbited our own Sun. And “dwarf planet” sounded like a Saturday morning cartoon begging for its own toy line.Continue Readi…
articles.summary: Rubin Observatory's advanced digital camera has discovered a new world beyond Pluto, showcasing the technological advances that continue to reveal hidden celestial bodies. The discovery reflects humanity's ongoing quest to map and understand the outer solar system.

articles.title: La Chine dévoile son plan pour un alunissage habité
articles.description: La Chine présente son calendrier ambitieux et précis pour envoyer ses taïkonautes sur la Lune avant la fin de la décennie.
articles.summary: China has unveiled an ambitious and detailed timeline for crewed lunar landings before the end of the decade. This milestone represents an inspiring expansion of humanity's efforts to return humans to the Moon.
